questions: For each i, are we allowed to choose any K elements that include A_i, or must we choose exactly K elements?
When choosing K elements that include A_i, can we choose the same element multiple times (with repetition) or must all chosen elements be distinct indices?
For each i, should we compute the maximum possible GCD over all such choices, the minimum possible GCD, or some other aggregation (like GCD of all possible choices)?
If multiple subsets yield the same GCD, is any specific tie-breaking required for output?
Are the chosen K elements required to be contiguous in the sequence, or can they be any K indices?

Does 'include A_i' mean A_i must be exactly one of the chosen elements, or does it mean the chosen multiset must contain at least one copy of the value A_i (possibly from a different index with same value)?
Should the output be N integers, one per i, each on a separate line, or space-separated on a single line?
Is the GCD defined as the greatest positive integer dividing all chosen elements, and if all chosen elements are zero, what is the GCD?
